title: The Matrix
blurb: Free your mind. Then GROUP BY it.

acts.prompt: This query should count the crew on each ship, but it only returns one row. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  ship,
  COUNT(*) AS crew_count
FROM crew;
acts.solution:
SELECT
  ship,
  COUNT(*) AS crew_count
FROM crew
GROUP BY ship;
acts.lesson: An aggregate next to a plain column needs GROUP BY on that column.

acts.prompt: Show the 3 best bullet-dodgers: name and bullets_dodged, most dodged first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  bullets_dodged
FROM crew
ORDER BY bullets_dodged DESC
LIMIT 3;
acts.lesson: ORDER BY ... DESC puts the biggest first; LIMIT keeps the top few.

acts.prompt: For every crew member show name, ship, and their rank on their own ship by bullets_dodged (1 = most dodged).
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  ship,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY ship ORDER BY bullets_dodged DESC) AS ship_rank
FROM crew;
acts.lesson: PARTITION BY restarts the ranking for each ship.

title: The Lord of the Rings
blurb: One query to rule them all.

acts.prompt: This query should list each race with more than one member in the fellowship, but it crashes. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  race,
  COUNT(*) AS members
FROM fellowship
WHERE COUNT(*) > 1
GROUP BY race;
acts.solution:
SELECT
  race,
  COUNT(*) AS members
FROM fellowship
GROUP BY race
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
acts.lesson: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters the groups afterwards.

acts.prompt: Show the average age of each race in the fellowship table: race and average age, oldest average first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  race,
  AVG(age) AS avg_age
FROM fellowship
GROUP BY race
ORDER BY avg_age DESC;
acts.lesson: GROUP BY makes one row per race; AVG works inside each group.

acts.prompt: Total orcs slain by each race: race and total orcs_slain, biggest total first. (The kills table has no race column.)
acts.solution:
SELECT
  f.race,
  SUM(k.orcs_slain) AS total
FROM fellowship f
JOIN kills k ON k.name = f.name
GROUP BY f.race
ORDER BY total DESC;
acts.lesson: JOIN on the shared name column, then group by the column you borrowed.

title: The Hobbit
blurb: An unexpected query.

acts.prompt: This query should list the items nobody has claimed yet, but it returns nothing. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  item
FROM hoard
WHERE claimed_by = NULL;
acts.solution:
SELECT
  item
FROM hoard
WHERE claimed_by IS NULL;
acts.lesson: Nothing ever equals NULL. Test for it with IS NULL.

acts.prompt: Show the 3 richest kinds of treasure: kind and total gold_value, richest first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  kind,
  SUM(gold_value) AS total
FROM hoard
GROUP BY kind
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 3;
acts.lesson: Group, sum, sort by the sum, then LIMIT.

acts.prompt: List every item with its gold_value, most valuable first, plus a running total of gold_value down the list.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  item,
  gold_value,
  SUM(gold_value) OVER (ORDER BY gold_value DESC) AS running_total
FROM hoard
ORDER BY gold_value DESC;
acts.lesson: SUM(...) OVER (ORDER BY ...) adds up everything so far in that order.

title: Cheaper by the Dozen
blurb: Twelve kids. One table. Okay, two.

acts.prompt: This query should show the name and age of every kid under 13, but it only returns one column. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  name age
FROM kids
WHERE age < 13;
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  age
FROM kids
WHERE age < 13;
acts.lesson: Without the comma, SQL reads "name age" as the name column renamed to age.

acts.prompt: Which hobbies are shared by 2 or more kids? Show hobby and number of kids, most popular first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  hobby,
  COUNT(*) AS kids
FROM kids
GROUP BY hobby
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
ORDER BY kids DESC;
acts.lesson: HAVING keeps only the groups that pass the test.

acts.prompt: Which kids have never logged a chore? Show just their name.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  k.name
FROM kids k
LEFT JOIN chore_log c ON c.name = k.name
WHERE c.name IS NULL;
acts.lesson: A LEFT JOIN keeps kids with no match; their chore columns come back NULL.

title: Jurassic Park
blurb: Life, uh, finds a WHERE clause.

acts.prompt: This query should show the species and headcount of every carnivore, but it crashes. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  species,
  headcount
FROM dinosaurs
WHERE diet = carnivore;
acts.solution:
SELECT
  species,
  headcount
FROM dinosaurs
WHERE diet = 'carnivore';
acts.lesson: Text values need single quotes. Without them SQL goes looking for a column called carnivore.

acts.prompt: How many animals are there of each diet? Show diet and total headcount, most animals first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  diet,
  SUM(headcount) AS total
FROM dinosaurs
GROUP BY diet
ORDER BY total DESC;
acts.lesson: SUM adds up the headcount column; COUNT would only count the rows.

acts.prompt: For every species show species, length_m, and the length of the longest dinosaur that shares its diet.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  species,
  length_m,
  MAX(length_m) OVER (PARTITION BY diet) AS longest_in_diet
FROM dinosaurs;
acts.lesson: A window function keeps every row and adds the group's value alongside it.

title: Titanic
blurb: Near, far, WHERE-ever you are.

acts.prompt: This query should list the name and age of every survivor (survived = 1), youngest first, but it crashes. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  name,
  age
FROM passengers
ORDER BY age
WHERE survived = 1;
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  age
FROM passengers
WHERE survived = 1
ORDER BY age;
acts.lesson: Clauses have a fixed order: WHERE comes before ORDER BY.

acts.prompt: For each class show class, number of passengers, and number of survivors.
acts.lesson: Summing a 0/1 column counts the 1s.

acts.prompt: For everyone who did not survive, show their name and the name of their deck, alphabetical by name.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  p.name,
  d.deck
FROM passengers p
JOIN decks d ON d.class = p.class
WHERE p.survived = 0
ORDER BY p.name;
acts.lesson: The class number links each passenger to a deck.

title: Home Alone
blurb: KEVIN! You forgot the ORDER BY!

acts.prompt: This query should return the single most painful trap, but it returns the least painful one. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  trap,
  pain
FROM traps
ORDER BY pain
LIMIT 1;
acts.solution:
SELECT
  trap,
  pain
FROM traps
ORDER BY pain DESC
LIMIT 1;
acts.lesson: ORDER BY sorts smallest first unless you add DESC.

acts.prompt: For each burglar show victim, number of traps they hit, and their total pain.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  victim,
  COUNT(*) AS traps_hit,
  SUM(pain) AS total_pain
FROM traps
GROUP BY victim;
acts.lesson: One GROUP BY can feed several aggregates at once.

acts.prompt: For every trap show step, victim, pain, and that victim's running total of pain so far (in step order).
acts.solution:
SELECT
  step,
  victim,
  pain,
  SUM(pain) OVER (PARTITION BY victim ORDER BY step) AS running_pain
FROM traps;
acts.lesson: PARTITION BY keeps a separate running total for each burglar.

title: Jaws
blurb: You're gonna need a bigger query.

acts.prompt: This query should count how many different beaches have had a sighting, but it counts every sighting. Fix it.
acts.lesson: COUNT(DISTINCT x) counts each different value once.

acts.prompt: Show the average reported length_ft at each beach: beach and average, biggest average first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  beach,
  AVG(length_ft) AS avg_length
FROM sightings
GROUP BY beach
ORDER BY avg_length DESC;
acts.lesson: You can ORDER BY the alias of an aggregate.

acts.prompt: For every sighting show id, length_ft, and the length_ft from the sighting before it (by id). The first sighting has nothing before it, so leave that NULL.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  id,
  length_ft,
  LAG(length_ft) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS previous_length
FROM sightings;
acts.lesson: LAG looks one row back in the window's order.

title: Back to the Future
blurb: Where we're going, we don't need rowids.

acts.prompt: This query should list the name and birth year of everyone in the McFly family, but it returns nothing. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  name,
  born
FROM citizens
WHERE name LIKE 'McFly';
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  born
FROM citizens
WHERE name LIKE '%McFly';
acts.lesson: LIKE without a % wildcard only matches the exact text.

acts.prompt: Show the 3 oldest citizens: name and their age in 1985, oldest first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  1985 - born AS age_in_1985
FROM citizens
ORDER BY born
LIMIT 3;
acts.lesson: You can do arithmetic right in the SELECT list.

acts.prompt: For each citizen who has time-traveled show name, job, and number of trips, most trips first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  c.name,
  c.job,
  COUNT(*) AS trip_count
FROM citizens c
JOIN trips t ON t.traveler = c.name
GROUP BY c.name, c.job
ORDER BY trip_count DESC;
acts.lesson: An inner JOIN drops citizens with no trips, which is what we want here.

title: Ocean's Eleven
blurb: Eleven rows. One vault.

acts.prompt: This query should list the name and specialty of every driver and every hacker, but it returns nothing. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  name,
  specialty
FROM crew
WHERE specialty = 'driver' AND specialty = 'hacker';
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  specialty
FROM crew
WHERE specialty = 'driver' OR specialty = 'hacker';
acts.lesson: No single row can be both. Use OR (or IN) to accept either value.

acts.prompt: The haul is $160 million and each member gets cut_pct percent of it. Show name and payout in millions for the 3 biggest payouts, biggest first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  160 * cut_pct / 100 AS payout_millions
FROM crew
ORDER BY payout_millions DESC
LIMIT 3;
acts.lesson: Compute the payout in SELECT, then sort by it.

acts.prompt: For every piece of gear costing more than 50 (thousand) show item, its owner's specialty, and cost_thousands, priciest first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  g.item,
  c.specialty,
  g.cost_thousands
FROM gear g
JOIN crew c ON c.name = g.owner
WHERE g.cost_thousands > 50
ORDER BY g.cost_thousands DESC;
acts.lesson: Join gear.owner to crew.name to borrow the specialty.

title: Star Wars
blurb: A long time ago, in a table far, far away.

acts.prompt: This query should show the total kills for each squadron, but the numbers are far too small. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  squadron,
  AVG(kills) AS total_kills
FROM pilots
GROUP BY squadron;
acts.solution:
SELECT
  squadron,
  SUM(kills) AS total_kills
FROM pilots
GROUP BY squadron;
acts.lesson: AVG gives the typical value; SUM adds them all up.

acts.prompt: Show the name and kills of every pilot who survived (survived = 1), most kills first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  kills
FROM pilots
WHERE survived = 1
ORDER BY kills DESC;
acts.lesson: Filter with WHERE first, then sort what is left.

acts.prompt: For every pilot show name, squadron, kills, and the total kills of their whole squadron.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  squadron,
  kills,
  SUM(kills) OVER (PARTITION BY squadron) AS squadron_kills
FROM pilots;
acts.lesson: SUM(...) OVER (PARTITION BY ...) puts the group total on every row.

title: Harry Potter
blurb: The query that lived.

acts.prompt: This query should list the name and house of every student in Gryffindor or Ravenclaw, but it crashes. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  name,
  house
FROM students
WHERE house IN 'Gryffindor', 'Ravenclaw';
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  house
FROM students
WHERE house IN ('Gryffindor', 'Ravenclaw');
acts.lesson: The list after IN has to be wrapped in parentheses.

acts.prompt: Show each house and its total points, highest total first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  house,
  SUM(points) AS total_points
FROM students
GROUP BY house
ORDER BY total_points DESC;
acts.lesson: Group by house, sum the points, sort by the sum.

acts.prompt: For each head of house show head_of_house and the total points their students earned, highest first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  h.head_of_house,
  SUM(s.points) AS total_points
FROM students s
JOIN houses h ON h.house = s.house
GROUP BY h.head_of_house
ORDER BY total_points DESC;
acts.lesson: Join on the house name, then group by the column you borrowed.

title: Toy Story
blurb: To infinity and GROUP BY-ond.

acts.prompt: This query should list each owner once, but it repeats them. Fix it.
acts.lesson: DISTINCT removes repeated rows from the result.

acts.prompt: Show the 3 oldest toys: name and year_made, oldest first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  year_made
FROM toys
ORDER BY year_made
LIMIT 3;
acts.lesson: ORDER BY sorts smallest first by default, which here means oldest.

acts.prompt: For every toy show name, owner, year_made, and the year_made of the oldest toy that has the same owner.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  owner,
  year_made,
  MIN(year_made) OVER (PARTITION BY owner) AS oldest_for_owner
FROM toys;
acts.lesson: MIN(...) OVER (PARTITION BY ...) finds the smallest value within each owner's toys.

title: Finding Nemo
blurb: Just keep querying.

acts.prompt: This query should list the name and species of everyone who is NOT a clownfish, but it lists only the clownfish. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  name,
  species
FROM fish
WHERE species = 'clownfish';
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  species
FROM fish
WHERE species != 'clownfish';
acts.lesson: = keeps the matches; != (or <>) keeps everything else.

acts.prompt: For each home show home and the number of fish living there.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  home,
  COUNT(*) AS fish_count
FROM fish
GROUP BY home;
acts.lesson: COUNT(*) with GROUP BY counts the rows in each group.

acts.prompt: For each place that has fish show place, distance_km, and the number of fish living there, farthest place first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  p.place,
  p.distance_km,
  COUNT(*) AS fish_count
FROM places p
JOIN fish f ON f.home = p.place
GROUP BY p.place, p.distance_km
ORDER BY p.distance_km DESC;
acts.lesson: An inner JOIN leaves out the Trench, because no fish matches it.

title: The Lion King
blurb: Hakuna ma-data.

acts.prompt: This query should list the name and weight_kg of animals weighing between 50 and 100 kg, but it returns nothing. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  name,
  weight_kg
FROM animals
WHERE weight_kg BETWEEN 100 AND 50;
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  weight_kg
FROM animals
WHERE weight_kg BETWEEN 50 AND 100;
acts.lesson: BETWEEN needs the smaller number first.

acts.prompt: For species with more than one animal, show species and average weight_kg, heaviest average first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  species,
  AVG(weight_kg) AS avg_weight
FROM animals
GROUP BY species
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY avg_weight DESC;
acts.lesson: HAVING filters groups after they are formed.

acts.prompt: For every animal show name, weight_kg, and its rank among all animals by weight (1 = heaviest).
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  weight_kg,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY weight_kg DESC) AS weight_rank
FROM animals;
acts.lesson: With no PARTITION BY, the ranking runs across the whole table.

title: Ghostbusters
blurb: Who you gonna query?

acts.prompt: This query should list the name and class of every ghost of class 6 or higher, but it crashes. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  name,
  class
FORM ghosts
WHERE class >= 6;
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  class
FROM ghosts
WHERE class >= 6;
acts.lesson: Keywords have to be spelled exactly: FROM, not FORM.

acts.prompt: Using the calls table, show each location that paid a fee and the total fee it paid, biggest total first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  location,
  SUM(fee) AS total_fee
FROM calls
WHERE fee > 0
GROUP BY location
ORDER BY total_fee DESC;
acts.lesson: WHERE drops the unpaid calls before the groups are added up.

acts.prompt: For every call about a ghost of class 6 or higher show call_id, location, and the ghost's class, in call_id order.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  c.call_id,
  c.location,
  g.class
FROM calls c
JOIN ghosts g ON g.name = c.ghost
WHERE g.class >= 6
ORDER BY c.call_id;
acts.lesson: Join calls.ghost to ghosts.name, then filter on the borrowed class.

title: Shrek
blurb: Queries are like onions. They have layers.

acts.prompt: This query should show only the 3 noisiest guests, but it shows everyone. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  name,
  noise_level
FROM swamp_guests
ORDER BY noise_level DESC;
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  noise_level
FROM swamp_guests
ORDER BY noise_level DESC
LIMIT 3;
acts.lesson: LIMIT cuts the result off after that many rows.

acts.prompt: Show the 3 noisiest kinds of guest: kind and average noise_level, noisiest first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  kind,
  AVG(noise_level) AS avg_noise
FROM swamp_guests
GROUP BY kind
ORDER BY avg_noise DESC
LIMIT 3;
acts.lesson: Group, average, sort by the average, then LIMIT.

acts.prompt: For every guest show name, noise_level, and the average noise_level of all guests (the same number on every row).
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  noise_level,
  AVG(noise_level) OVER () AS avg_noise
FROM swamp_guests;
acts.lesson: An empty OVER () treats the whole table as one window.

title: Raiders of the Lost Ark
blurb: It belongs in a database!

acts.prompt: This query should list artifacts from most valuable to least, but it sorts them by name instead. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  artifact,
  value_thousands
FROM artifacts
ORDER BY artifact DESC;
acts.solution:
SELECT
  artifact,
  value_thousands
FROM artifacts
ORDER BY value_thousands DESC;
acts.lesson: ORDER BY sorts by whichever column you name, so name the right one.

acts.prompt: Using the sites table, show each country and its total number of traps, most traps first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  country,
  SUM(traps) AS total_traps
FROM sites
GROUP BY country
ORDER BY total_traps DESC;
acts.lesson: Two sites share a country, so their traps are added together.

acts.prompt: Show each country and the total value_thousands of the artifacts found there, richest first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  s.country,
  SUM(a.value_thousands) AS total_value
FROM artifacts a
JOIN sites s ON s.site = a.site
GROUP BY s.country
ORDER BY total_value DESC;
acts.lesson: The site name links each artifact to a country.

title: Monsters, Inc.
blurb: We scare because we query.

acts.prompt: This query should show one row per floor with its total screams, but it returns a row for every scarer. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  floor,
  SUM(screams) AS total_screams
FROM scarers
GROUP BY name;
acts.solution:
SELECT
  floor,
  SUM(screams) AS total_screams
FROM scarers
GROUP BY floor;
acts.lesson: Group by the thing you want one row for.

acts.prompt: Show the name and screams of scarers on floor E or G with more than 500 screams, most screams first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  screams
FROM scarers
WHERE floor IN ('E', 'G')
  AND screams > 500
ORDER BY screams DESC;
acts.lesson: AND combines two conditions; IN checks a column against a list.

acts.prompt: Rank the scarers by screams, most first. For every scarer show name, screams, and the screams of the scarer ranked just above them (NULL for the leader).
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  screams,
  LAG(screams) OVER (ORDER BY screams DESC) AS next_above
FROM scarers;
acts.lesson: LAG reads the previous row in the window's order.

title: Top Gun
blurb: I feel the need. The need for speedy queries.

acts.prompt: This query should return a single number, how many pilots there are, but it lists them instead. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  callsign
FROM aviators
WHERE role = 'pilot';
acts.solution:
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS pilot_count
FROM aviators
WHERE role = 'pilot';
acts.lesson: COUNT(*) collapses the matching rows into one number.

acts.prompt: Using the hops table, show the 3 highest-scoring winners: winner and total points, highest first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  winner,
  SUM(points) AS total_points
FROM hops
GROUP BY winner
ORDER BY total_points DESC
LIMIT 3;
acts.lesson: Add up each winner's hops, sort, and keep the top 3.

acts.prompt: Show each role and the total hop points won by aviators in that role, highest first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  a.role,
  SUM(h.points) AS total_points
FROM hops h
JOIN aviators a ON a.callsign = h.winner
GROUP BY a.role
ORDER BY total_points DESC;
acts.lesson: Join the winner's callsign to find their role, then group by role.

title: The Wizard of Oz
blurb: There's no place like SELECT *.

acts.prompt: This query should list the place and who joined at every stop where somebody joined, but it returns nothing. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  place,
  joined
FROM road
WHERE joined != NULL;
acts.solution:
SELECT
  place,
  joined
FROM road
WHERE joined IS NOT NULL;
acts.lesson: Comparing with NULL never works, even with !=. Use IS NOT NULL.

acts.prompt: Show the 3 longest stretches of road: place and miles, longest first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  place,
  miles
FROM road
ORDER BY miles DESC
LIMIT 3;
acts.lesson: Sort biggest first, then LIMIT to the top few.

acts.prompt: For every stop show stop, place, miles, and the running total of miles walked so far (in stop order).
acts.solution:
SELECT
  stop,
  place,
  miles,
  SUM(miles) OVER (ORDER BY stop) AS miles_so_far
FROM road;
acts.lesson: SUM(...) OVER (ORDER BY ...) keeps a running total.

title: Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory
blurb: Come with me, and you'll be in a world of pure aggregation.

acts.prompt: This query should return the largest number of oompa_loompas working in any one room, but it returns the smallest. Fix it.
acts.lesson: MIN finds the smallest value, MAX the largest.

acts.prompt: Using the rooms table, show room and oompa_loompas for rooms with more than 4 oompa loompas, in tour order (minutes_in_tour).
acts.solution:
SELECT
  room,
  oompa_loompas
FROM rooms
WHERE oompa_loompas > 4
ORDER BY minutes_in_tour;
acts.lesson: You can sort by a column you are not showing.

acts.prompt: For each child show name and the hazard of the room they were in, in the order the tour reaches those rooms (minutes_in_tour).
acts.solution:
SELECT
  c.name,
  r.hazard
FROM children c
JOIN rooms r ON r.room = c.room
ORDER BY r.minutes_in_tour;
acts.lesson: Join on the room name to borrow columns from rooms.

title: The Incredibles
blurb: No capes. No cross joins.

acts.prompt: This query should list the name and missions of every super with at least 80 missions, but it leaves one out. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  name,
  missions
FROM supers
WHERE missions > 80;
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  missions
FROM supers
WHERE missions >= 80;
acts.lesson: "At least 80" includes 80 itself: use >=, not >.

acts.prompt: For each status show status, the number of supers, and their total missions.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  status,
  COUNT(*) AS supers,
  SUM(missions) AS total_missions
FROM supers
GROUP BY status;
acts.lesson: One GROUP BY can feed a count and a sum at once.

acts.prompt: For every super show name, status, missions, and their rank by missions among supers with the same status (1 = most).
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  status,
  missions,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY status ORDER BY missions DESC) AS status_rank
FROM supers;
acts.lesson: PARTITION BY restarts the ranking for each status.

title: Pirates of the Caribbean
blurb: The schema is more what you'd call guidelines.

acts.prompt: This query should list the name and ship of everyone whose name starts with M, but it finds nobody. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  name,
  ship
FROM crew
WHERE name LIKE '%M';
acts.solution:
SELECT
  name,
  ship
FROM crew
WHERE name LIKE 'M%';
acts.lesson: The % stands for "anything": put it after the M to match names that start with it.

acts.prompt: Using the crew table, show the 3 richest roles: role and total doubloons, richest first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  role,
  SUM(doubloons) AS total_doubloons
FROM crew
GROUP BY role
ORDER BY total_doubloons DESC
LIMIT 3;
acts.lesson: Group, sum, sort by the sum, then LIMIT.

acts.prompt: For each captain show captain and the total doubloons held by their crew, richest first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  s.captain,
  SUM(c.doubloons) AS total_doubloons
FROM crew c
JOIN ships s ON s.ship = c.ship
GROUP BY s.captain
ORDER BY total_doubloons DESC;
acts.lesson: The ship name links each sailor to a captain.

title: Frozen
blurb: Let it GROUP. Let it GROUP.

acts.prompt: This query should return the single biggest snowfall (place and snowfall_cm), but it just returns the first row in the table. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  place,
  snowfall_cm
FROM storms
LIMIT 1;
acts.solution:
SELECT
  place,
  snowfall_cm
FROM storms
ORDER BY snowfall_cm DESC
LIMIT 1;
acts.lesson: LIMIT 1 only means "the biggest" if you sort first.

acts.prompt: Show each place and its total snowfall_cm, snowiest first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  place,
  SUM(snowfall_cm) AS total_snow
FROM storms
GROUP BY place
ORDER BY total_snow DESC;
acts.lesson: Group by place, sum the snowfall, sort by the sum.

acts.prompt: For every row show day, place, snowfall_cm, and the snowfall_cm at that same place on its previous recorded day (NULL if there is none).
acts.solution:
SELECT
  day,
  place,
  snowfall_cm,
  LAG(snowfall_cm) OVER (PARTITION BY place ORDER BY day) AS previous_snow
FROM storms;
acts.lesson: LAG with PARTITION BY looks back within each place separately.

title: Jumanji
blurb: Roll the dice, then ORDER BY them.

acts.prompt: This query should show how many turns each player has taken, but it adds up their dice instead. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  player,
  SUM(roll) AS turns
FROM rolls
GROUP BY player;
acts.solution:
SELECT
  player,
  COUNT(*) AS turns
FROM rolls
GROUP BY player;
acts.lesson: SUM adds up a column's values; COUNT(*) counts the rows.

acts.prompt: Using the rolls table, show the 3 highest rolls: player, roll, and hazard, highest first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  player,
  roll,
  hazard
FROM rolls
ORDER BY roll DESC
LIMIT 3;
acts.lesson: ORDER BY ... DESC with LIMIT gives the top few.

acts.prompt: Show each token and the total of all rolls made by its player, highest total first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  p.token,
  SUM(r.roll) AS total_rolled
FROM rolls r
JOIN players p ON p.player = r.player
GROUP BY p.token
ORDER BY total_rolled DESC;
acts.lesson: Join on the player name, then group by the token you borrowed.

title: The Princess Bride
blurb: As you wish. As you WHERE.

acts.prompt: This query should show each challenge and how long it took in hours, as a decimal, but every answer comes out as 0 or 1. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  challenge,
  minutes / 60 AS hours
FROM quest;
acts.solution:
SELECT
  challenge,
  minutes / 60.0 AS hours
FROM quest;
acts.lesson: Dividing two whole numbers throws away the remainder. Make one of them a decimal.

acts.prompt: Show challenge, opponent, and minutes for every challenge longer than 15 minutes, longest first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  challenge,
  opponent,
  minutes
FROM quest
WHERE minutes > 15
ORDER BY minutes DESC;
acts.lesson: Filter with WHERE, then sort what is left.

acts.prompt: For every step show step, challenge, minutes, and the minutes of the next challenge (NULL for the last one).
acts.solution:
SELECT
  step,
  challenge,
  minutes,
  LEAD(minutes) OVER (ORDER BY step) AS next_minutes
FROM quest;
acts.lesson: LEAD looks one row ahead; LAG looks one row back.

title: Men in Black
blurb: The last suit you'll ever JOIN.

acts.prompt: This query should list every alien and its threat, most dangerous first, but it crashes. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  alien,
  threat
FROM aliens
ORDER BY treat DESC;
acts.solution:
SELECT
  alien,
  threat
FROM aliens
ORDER BY threat DESC;
acts.lesson: A misspelled column name is an error: SQL has no column called treat.

acts.prompt: Using the cases table, show each agent and the total number of people they neuralyzed, most first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  agent,
  SUM(neuralyzed) AS total_neuralyzed
FROM cases
GROUP BY agent
ORDER BY total_neuralyzed DESC;
acts.lesson: Group by agent, sum, and sort by the sum.

acts.prompt: For every case about an alien with a threat of 4 or higher show case_id, agent, and the alien's disguise, in case_id order.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  c.case_id,
  c.agent,
  a.disguise
FROM cases c
JOIN aliens a ON a.alien = c.alien
WHERE a.threat >= 4
ORDER BY c.case_id;
acts.lesson: Join on the alien's name, then filter on the borrowed threat column.

title: Ratatouille
blurb: Anyone can query.

acts.prompt: This query should list mains and desserts that cost under 20 euros, but expensive mains are showing up too. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  dish,
  course,
  price_euros
FROM dishes
WHERE course = 'main' OR course = 'dessert'
  AND price_euros < 20;
acts.solution:
SELECT
  dish,
  course,
  price_euros
FROM dishes
WHERE (course = 'main' OR course = 'dessert')
  AND price_euros < 20;
acts.lesson: AND is applied before OR. Parentheses make the OR happen first.

acts.prompt: For chefs with at least 2 dishes, show chef and their average stars, best first.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  chef,
  AVG(stars) AS avg_stars
FROM dishes
GROUP BY chef
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
ORDER BY avg_stars DESC;
acts.lesson: HAVING keeps only the chefs with enough dishes.

acts.prompt: For every dish show dish, course, price_euros, and the average price_euros of all dishes in the same course.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  dish,
  course,
  price_euros,
  AVG(price_euros) OVER (PARTITION BY course) AS course_avg
FROM dishes;
acts.lesson: AVG(...) OVER (PARTITION BY ...) puts each course's average on every row.

title: Rocky
blurb: Yo, Adrian! It returned rows!

acts.prompt: This query should count the fights for each result (win, loss, draw), but it only returns one row. Fix it.
acts.starter:
SELECT
  result,
  COUNT(*) AS fight_count
FROM fights;
acts.solution:
SELECT
  result,
  COUNT(*) AS fight_count
FROM fights
GROUP BY result;
acts.lesson: An aggregate next to a plain column needs GROUP BY on that column.

acts.prompt: Which opponents did Rocky fight more than once? Show opponent and the number of fights.
acts.solution:
SELECT
  opponent,
  COUNT(*) AS fight_count
FROM fights
GROUP BY opponent
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
acts.lesson: HAVING filters on the count after grouping.

acts.prompt: For every fight show fight_no, opponent, and which meeting with that opponent it was (1 for the first time they fought, 2 for the second).
acts.solution:
SELECT
  fight_no,
  opponent,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY opponent ORDER BY fight_no) AS meeting
FROM fights;
acts.lesson: ROW_NUMBER numbers the rows inside each partition, starting again at 1.
